body:
`html-escape` is only used in SSR.
We use `document::create_text_node()` in browsers where escaping is managed by browsers.

Are you experiencing this with SSR?
I was only able to reproduce it in SSR
Yes, this is an SSR issue. I wanted to ship the critical css in the document head. I ended up adding more class to make it work. But using the child combinator would have been nicer.

body:
This is unrelated to html-escape, as html-escape does not even get a chance to know what tag it is working on.

https://github.com/yewstack/yew/blob/e59edde1d0c201c75cbae0d581795ad9a1c6a4c1/packages/yew/src/virtual_dom/vtext.rs#L57

This is called for every text node, regardless of the tag it that is currently being rendered. `style` and `script` need to be special cases, with their own escape functions from `html-escape`. This requires keeping track of what tag is being rendered, which we currently do not do. 

@fabien-h are you still interested in fixing this? I would be happy to look at any PRs fixing this bug

I have a clear idea of how to fix this issue, and I have 2 solutions in mind for this: we can either make the parser aware of the special characteristics of `<style>` & `<script>` tags and prohibit providing anything other than 0 or 1 VText nodes to these tags, or we can leave the semantics of these elements as they are and just pass the current inner-most VTag's name to `render_into_stream` functions as context, so that this context can be used in `VText::render_into_stream` to choose between `encode_text`, `encode_style` & `encode_script` functions of the `html_escape` module. What would be the best approach in this situation?
Yes, I'll start working on it shortly
